page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.large is a virtual server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance delivers 4 vCPUs backed by 2 physical CPU cores with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). This configuration operates on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU core allocation. It features no local disk storage, requiring network-attached volumes for data persistence, and includes zero onboard GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Across compute and throughput benchmarks, the instance demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Stress-ng scores register at 1106.18 for single-core and 4400.61 for multi-core computation, placing the CPU throughput within the lower quartile of tracked platforms. Geekbench yields 929.0 for single-core and 2969.0 for multi-core execution, with software compilation reaching 4680.0. Memory subsystems report uncached large-block write performance of 29.39 GB/sec, reflecting moderate throughput, while uncached read bandwidth reaches 34.59 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 CPU-to-memory profile and modest benchmark outputs, the ecs.n1.large represents an entry compute resource. The lack of integrated high-speed NVMe storage and entry-tier compression speeds indicate reduced efficiency for intense I/O or low-latency transactional databases. The instance remains suitable for lightweight web hosting, background batch jobs, staging environments, and basic CI/CD build tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.large is an entry-tier x86_64 instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The system provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with 8.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage, GPUs, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark results position the server in the lower quartile for compute throughput, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 2969.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5282.4. Memory write bandwidth performs moderately at 29.39 GB/sec on uncached 256MB operations, while Redis SET throughput achieves 5.51 million operations per second. The instance is suited for non-critical workloads, such as lightweight web serving, staging servers, and routine background task processing.
